VersionInfo.Content: Currently loaded Dungeon World Automation Toolkit version.

ModuleVersion.Name: Dungeon World Automation Toolkit Version
ModuleVersion.Label: Check Version
ModuleVersion.Hint: Shows the version of this module currently loaded (informational).

EnableNpcGenerator.Name: Enable NPC Generator
EnableNpcGenerator.Hint: Adds a tab to NPC sheets that randomly rolls a name, instinct, and trait.

EnableMonsterGenerator.Name: Enable Monster Stat Generator
EnableMonsterGenerator.Hint: Adds a tab to NPC sheets that randomly rolls a damage die, armor, HP, and coin.

EnableAttackAssistant.Name: Enable Attack Damage Automation
EnableAttackAssistant.Hint: On a success or partial success, asks whether to roll damage and automatically deducts consumables like ammo. Which moves trigger this is managed in the name lists below and the Special Attack Moves setting.

MeleeMoveNames.Name: Melee Move Names
MeleeMoveNames.Hint: Melee moves like Hack & Slash that always roll damage on success/partial with no choices involved (comma separated). Adjust this if a translation module renamed the move. Moves whose behavior depends on a choice (like Backstab) are managed separately in Special Attack Moves.

RangedMoveNames.Name: Ranged Move Names
RangedMoveNames.Hint: Ranged moves like Volley that always roll damage on success/partial with no choices involved (comma separated). These also trigger the ammo consumption prompt. Moves whose behavior depends on a choice (like Called Shot) are managed separately in Special Attack Moves.

MeleeWeaponTags.Name: Melee Weapon Tags
MeleeWeaponTags.Hint: If a weapon's tags contain any of these keywords (comma separated), it's treated as melee. Weapons have no explicit melee/ranged field; this relies on the Dungeon World convention that melee weapons use hand/close/reach. A weapon matching neither this list nor Ranged Weapon Tags still shows up in the weapon picker (it isn't excluded).

RangedWeaponTags.Name: Ranged Weapon Tags
RangedWeaponTags.Hint: If a weapon's tags contain any of these keywords (comma separated), it's treated as ranged. Dungeon World's convention is that ranged weapons use near/far. Default: near, far.

TagMenu.Name: Damage Tag Automation
TagMenu.Label: Edit Tag List
TagMenu.Hint: Individually toggle which weapon tags are automatically applied when rolling damage.

AttackMovesMenu.Name: Special Attack Moves
AttackMovesMenu.Label: Edit Special Attack Moves
AttackMovesMenu.Hint: Register/edit attack moves whose damage depends on a choice, like Backstab or Called Shot, by name, ranged flag, and behavior. Defaults to the English names (Backstab, Called Shot); edit the name field if your game uses a translated name.

EnableSpellcastingAssistant.Name: Enable Spellcasting Assistant
EnableSpellcastingAssistant.Hint: On a success or partial success for a Cast a Spell-type move, asks which prepared spell was used, tracks ongoing spells, and applies a penalty to the next casting.

CastSpellMoveNames.Name: Cast Spell Move Names
CastSpellMoveNames.Hint: The Cleric/Wizard "Cast a Spell" move names (comma separated, translated if applicable). Defaults to the English originals (Cast A Spell, Cast a Spell).

OngoingSpellsMenu.Name: Ongoing Spells
OngoingSpellsMenu.Label: Edit Ongoing Spells
OngoingSpellsMenu.Hint: Register/edit which spells affect future spellcasting rolls while maintained, by name and penalty type. Spells not listed are treated as one-shot.

SpellAugmentationMoveNames.Name: Spell Augmentation Move Names
SpellAugmentationMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated) that let the caster end an ongoing spell to add its level to damage dealt. Only asked when the actor has this move and an active ongoing spell.

CastPartialRevokeIndex.Name: Cast Spell Partial - Revoke Option Number
CastPartialRevokeIndex.Hint: Which numbered choice in the Cast a Spell partial-success list is "the spell is revoked (unusable until you commune/prepare spells again)"? Position 3 in the default Dungeon World text. Set to 0 to disable this effect.

CastPartialPenaltyIndex.Name: Cast Spell Partial - Penalty Option Number
CastPartialPenaltyIndex.Hint: Which numbered choice in the Cast a Spell partial-success list is "-1 to cast a spell until you commune/prepare spells again"? Position 2 in the default Dungeon World text. Set to 0 to disable this effect.

TranslationImportMenu.Name: Auto-fill from Translation Module
TranslationImportMenu.Label: Open Auto-fill Tool
TranslationImportMenu.Hint: If the Nomal-1/dungeonworld-ko Korean translation module is installed, fill in the move/spell name settings above using its translation data instead of typing them by hand.

EnableHitTriggerAssistant.Name: Enable Hit-Taken Automation
EnableHitTriggerAssistant.Hint: When a player character's HP is about to drop, asks whether to negate the damage using a move like Armor Mastery or Bloody Aegis (at the cost of armor or a debility) before the HP change is applied. Which moves qualify is managed in the Hit-Taken Moves setting below.

HitTriggerMovesMenu.Name: Hit-Taken Moves
HitTriggerMovesMenu.Label: Edit Hit-Taken Moves
HitTriggerMovesMenu.Hint: Register/edit moves that can negate incoming damage at a cost, by name and effect (lower armor by 1, or take a debility of your choice). Choosing "lower armor by 1" asks which equipped armor item takes the durability hit, reducing its armor tag by 1 (destroying it if it hits 0) — if nothing is equipped, only the character's armor value is lowered. "Grants +1 forward" is for moves like Armored Perfection that also grant a bonus on top of negating the damage.

IndomitableMoveNames.Name: Indomitable Move Names
IndomitableMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated) that grant +1 forward whenever the character takes a new debility, for any reason (including from Bloody Aegis).

EnableHealingAssistant.Name: Enable Healing Automation
EnableHealingAssistant.Hint: On a success or partial success for a healing move (Lay On Hands), or when a healing spell (Cure Light/Moderate/Critical Wounds, Heal) is cast via the Cast a Spell flow, asks who to heal and rolls (or asks for) the amount, then applies it. The recipient can be anyone the healer at least has observer access to (handy for narratively-ambiguous allies/enemies); if the healer doesn't have full access, an online GM is asked to approve before it's applied. Which moves/spells qualify is managed in the Healing Moves setting below.

HealingMovesMenu.Name: Healing Moves
HealingMovesMenu.Label: Edit Healing Moves
HealingMovesMenu.Hint: Register/edit moves and spells that heal, by name and how to determine the amount: automatically (reads the spell's own roll formula, or an inline dice notation like [[1d8]] in the move's own text), a custom formula you type in, or "up to max HP" (prompts for a number, for Heal). Check "Transfer to self on partial" for moves like Lay On Hands whose partial-success result transfers the healing (or disease) to the healer instead.

HospitallerMovesMenu.Name: Hospitaller Moves
HospitallerMovesMenu.Label: Edit Hospitaller Moves
HospitallerMovesMenu.Hint: Register moves like Hospitaller/Perfect Hospitaller that add extra healing whenever the character heals someone else (not themselves), by name and bonus dice formula.

EnableMoveUpgradeAssistant.Name: Enable Move Upgrade Automation
EnableMoveUpgradeAssistant.Hint: When a character learns an advanced move that upgrades an earlier one (e.g. Perfect Hospitaller upgrading Hospitaller), automatically removes the earlier move from the sheet. Which pairs count is managed in the Move Upgrades setting below.

MoveUpgradesMenu.Name: Move Upgrades
MoveUpgradesMenu.Label: Edit Move Upgrades
MoveUpgradesMenu.Hint: Register pairs of an upgrade move and its prerequisite move. With "Removes Prerequisite" checked, learning the upgrade automatically deletes the prerequisite; unchecked, the prerequisite stays (a "requires" relationship rather than a "replaces" one). Pre-filled with all 43 such pairs found across the 8 core classes' compendium data (each advanced move's own "requires" field), all with removal checked by default — uncheck any pair you find is actually a "requires" relationship.

DamageReductionMovesMenu.Name: Conditional Armor Bonus Moves
DamageReductionMovesMenu.Label: Edit Conditional Armor Bonus Moves
DamageReductionMovesMenu.Hint: Register moves like Underdog/Serious Underdog (outnumbered) or Bark Skin (feet on the ground) that grant an armor bonus based on a condition independent of any other move/state, by name, base bonus, and bonus when the condition is met. Each move gets its own independent per-character toggle (see the move's sheet badges), and the armor recalculation button reflects all of them.

ConditionalDamageMovesMenu.Name: Conditional Damage Moves
ConditionalDamageMovesMenu.Label: Edit Conditional Damage Moves
ConditionalDamageMovesMenu.Hint: Register moves like Smite/Holy Smite/Exterminatus or Viper's Strike/Fangs that add a dice bonus (or penalty) to a damage roll depending on a fictional condition that can't be auto-detected (being on a Quest, dual-wielding, etc.) — asked as Y/N when rolling damage. "Yes"/"No" formula are added to the roll; leave a formula blank or "0" to add nothing for that answer. Check "Requires Designation" for moves like Exterminatus whose effect doesn't exist at all until a target is declared (adds a designated/not-designated toggle on the sheet; while not designated, the move is completely ignored).

ConditionalTagMovesMenu.Name: Conditional Damage Tag Moves
ConditionalTagMovesMenu.Label: Edit Conditional Damage Tag Moves
ConditionalTagMovesMenu.Hint: Register moves like Ranger Smaug's Belly that add a literal damage tag (e.g. "2 piercing") to this attack whenever a fictional condition that can't be auto-detected (knowing the target's weakest point, etc.) is met — asked as Y/N when rolling damage. On "yes", the registered tag text is shown verbatim in the damage message (the dungeonworld system's damage-apply button picks it up automatically). "No" adds nothing.

SuperiorWarriorMoveNames.Name: Superior Warrior Move Names
SuperiorWarriorMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated) that announce in chat whenever a melee attack move reaches an extreme success (12+).

SmashMoveNames.Name: Smash! Move Names
SmashMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated, default: Smash!) that announce "choose something physical they have and they lose it" in chat whenever a melee attack move reaches an extreme success (12+).

MuscleboundMoveNames.Name: Musclebound Move Names
MuscleboundMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated, default: Musclebound) that always add the forceful/messy note text to a character's damage messages, regardless of the actual weapon's tags. Both tags must also be enabled in the damage tag display settings to show up.

EnableDruidAssistant.Name: Enable Druid Assistant
EnableDruidAssistant.Hint: Adds a character sheet tab for Druids showing a Balance counter (gained whenever the character deals damage via the automated attack flow, spendable to heal someone) and Shapeshift state (active/inactive, current animal form, and a free-text note area for the GM).

DruidBalanceMoveNames.Name: Druid Balance Move Names
DruidBalanceMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated) whose owner gains 1 Balance whenever they deal damage through this module's attack automation.

DruidShapeshifterMoveNames.Name: Druid Shapeshifter Move Names
DruidShapeshifterMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated) that, on a success or partial success, ask for the new animal form's name and mark the character as shapeshifted. Also auto-sets Hold from the move's own result text (e.g. "Hold 3").

DruidDamageDieMovesMenu.Name: Druid Shapeshift Damage Die Settings
DruidDamageDieMovesMenu.Label: Edit Shapeshift Damage Dice
DruidDamageDieMovesMenu.Hint: Register moves like Red of Tooth and Claw/Blood and Thunder that upgrade the damage die while shapeshifted, by name and die size. Only applies while shapeshifted; otherwise a chat note explains it wasn't applied.

DruidShedMoveNames.Name: Druid Shed Move Names
DruidShedMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated) that let the character revert to natural form to negate damage taken while shapeshifted. Appears as an option in the incoming-damage negation dialog, and only shows up while shapeshifted.

DruidFormcrafterMoveNames.Name: Druid Formcrafter Move Names
DruidFormcrafterMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated) that grant +1 ongoing to a player-chosen ability and -1 ongoing to a GM-chosen ability while shapeshifted. Moves that use a fixed ability score (e.g. melee moves) apply automatically; moves like Defy Danger that let you pick the ability at roll time ask for the ability via this module's own dialog first (instead of the system's), then apply the bonus/penalty for whichever ability was chosen.

DruidFormshaperMoveNames.Name: Druid Formshaper Move Names
DruidFormshaperMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated) that let the character choose +1 armor or +1d4 damage each time they shapeshift.

EnableNoteMoves.Name: Enable Note-Taking Moves
EnableNoteMoves.Hint: For moves like Deity/Apotheosis/Animal Companion/Quest/Born of the Soil that ask the player to freely define something (a god's name and domain, a chosen land, etc.) rather than roll dice, actually triggering the move (clicking it in the move list) shows a prompt with the choices found in the move's own description (plus a custom option), if any — then adds a tab named after the move with its description and a free-text note area. Moves with no such list in their description skip straight to the tab. Which moves qualify is managed in the Note-Taking Move Names setting below.

NoteMoveNames.Name: Note-Taking Move Names
NoteMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated) that get their own character-sheet tab (named after the move) with a free-text note area once actually triggered, for moves whose "mechanic" is really a narrative choice with no dice involved.

NoteMovesMenu.Name: Note-Taking Move Names
NoteMovesMenu.Label: Edit Note-Taking Move Names
NoteMovesMenu.Hint: Manage, as a list (instead of a comma-separated field), the move names that get their own free-text note tab once triggered — Deity, Animal Companion, Quest, Born of the Soil, and similar narrative-choice moves. Enter names exactly as they appear in your game (translated, if applicable).

EnableArmorAssistant.Name: Enable Armor Recalculation Button
EnableArmorAssistant.Hint: Turns the character sheet's 'Armor' label into a clickable button, like Damage. Clicking it overwrites the armor value with the sum of armor tags on currently equipped armor items, plus any currently active module modifiers (like Formshaper's 'armor' choice while shapeshifted). Hovering shows what goes into that total. The base system never auto-calculates armor — it's just a plain number field — so the field remains directly editable even with this button enabled.

EnableClassGrantAssistant.Name: Enable Class Grant Moves
EnableClassGrantAssistant.Hint: For moves like Paladin's Divine Favor or Ranger's God Amidst The Wastes that grant specific moves from another class outright when taken, actually triggering the move (clicking it in the move list) looks up the registered move(s) by name across all 8 core class compendiums and adds them automatically. Won't add a move the character already has. Which move grants what is managed in the Class Grant Moves setting below.

ClassGrantMovesMenu.Name: Class Grant Moves
ClassGrantMovesMenu.Label: Edit Class Grant Moves
ClassGrantMovesMenu.Hint: Register moves that grant specific move(s) from another class outright when triggered, by name and a comma-separated list of granted move names. Granted moves are looked up by name across all 8 core class compendiums (no need to specify which class).

EnableSpellPreparationAssistant.Name: Enable Spell Preparation Assistant
EnableSpellPreparationAssistant.Hint: For moves like the Wizard's Prepare Spells or the Cleric's Commune ("spend time in quiet contemplation, lose all currently prepared spells, and choose new ones"), actually triggering the move pops up a picker. The total level of chosen spells cannot exceed (character level + 1), and level-0 spells (cantrips/rotes) don't count against that limit and are always prepared automatically. Which moves work this way is managed in the Prepare Spells Moves setting below.

PrepareSpellsMovesMenu.Name: Prepare Spells Moves
PrepareSpellsMovesMenu.Label: Edit Prepare Spells Moves
PrepareSpellsMovesMenu.Hint: Register moves that work by "spend time in contemplation, lose all prepared spells, choose new ones" by name. Enabling "Enforce Individual Level Cap" (per the Cleric's Commune text) also excludes any spell of a higher level than the character's own level from the picker entirely (the Wizard's Prepare Spells has no such cap).

EnableSpellDiscountAssistant.Name: Enable Spell Discount Assistant
EnableSpellDiscountAssistant.Hint: Actually triggering the Wizard's Prodigy/Master or the Cleric's Chosen One/Anointed (all four share identical text) prompts you to pick one of your spellbook spells, and from then on that spell is treated as one level lower when computing the Prepare Spells budget (a level-1 spell becomes 0, i.e. always free like a cantrip). Which move names work this way is managed in the Spell Discount Move Names setting below.

DiscountSpellMoveNames.Name: Spell Discount Move Names
DiscountSpellMoveNames.Hint: Comma separated (default: Prodigy, Master, Chosen One, Anointed).

EnableSpellbookExpansionAssistant.Name: Enable Spellbook Expansion Assistant
EnableSpellbookExpansionAssistant.Hint: Actually triggering the Wizard's Expanded Spellbook prompts you to pick a class (Cleric/Wizard) and then a spell from that class's list, adding it outright to your spellbook (spells you already have are excluded). The added spell starts unprepared — you'll need to Prepare Spells again to actually use it. Which move names work this way is managed in the Expanded Spellbook Move Names setting below.

EnableCounterspellAssistant.Name: Enable Counterspell Assistant
EnableCounterspellAssistant.Hint: Actually triggering the Wizard's Counterspell/Protective Counter prompts you to pick which prepared spell to stake, then this module rolls 2d6+INT itself (including forward/ongoing) to resolve it — this move's compendium data has no roll type, so it can't go through the system's own automatic roll path. On a partial (7-9) the staked spell is forgotten (same consumption as a partial Cast a Spell). Which move names work this way is managed in the Counterspell Move Names setting below.

OngoingPenaltyReductionMovesMenu.Name: Ongoing Penalty Reduction Moves
OngoingPenaltyReductionMovesMenu.Label: Edit Ongoing Penalty Reduction Moves
OngoingPenaltyReductionMovesMenu.Hint: Register moves like the Cleric's Serenity/Providence ("ignore some of the cast-a-spell penalty from ongoing spells") by name and a reduction amount. This amount is subtracted from the total ongoing-spell penalty (floored at 0, and never applied to the vow penalty).

EmpowerMovesMenu.Name: Empower Moves
EmpowerMovesMenu.Label: Edit Empower Moves
EmpowerMovesMenu.Hint: Register moves like the Wizard's Empowered Magic/Greater Empowered Magic or the Cleric's Empower/Greater Empower ("on a successful cast, pay a cost to pick an extra effect") by name and whether it's the Greater version. Enabling "Greater" makes the effect free (no demerit) on an extreme success (12+).

HoldGrantMovesMenu.Name: Hold Grant Moves
HoldGrantMovesMenu.Label: Edit Hold Grant Moves
HoldGrantMovesMenu.Hint: Register moves like the Cleric's Divine Intervention/Divine Invincibility ("gain hold when you Commune, losing any hold you already had") by name and hold amount. This hold ties into the "Effect: Spend hold" option in the Hit-Taken Moves setting.

EnableCommandAssistant.Name: Enable Command Automation
EnableCommandAssistant.Hint: If the character has the Ranger's Command move, a "Cooperating" toggle badge appears next to it on the character sheet. While toggled on, the animal companion's stats (Ferocity/Cunning/Armor) are automatically applied to attack damage, certain rolls, and armor recalculation — the animal's stats are read automatically from the answer chosen when Animal Companion was activated. Instinct ("when another PC interferes with you") can't be auto-applied since the dungeonworld system doesn't let external bonuses affect a Bond roll — instead, if "Aid or Interfere Automation" is enabled, a popup asks the GM to tell the interfering player to add the Instinct bonus by hand right before they roll.

CommandCunningMoveNames.Name: Moves That Receive the Animal's Cunning
CommandCunningMoveNames.Hint: Moves like Hunt & Track/Discern Realities/Parley where "the animal's cunning is added to the roll" (comma-separated). Default is the English original names (Hunt & Track, Discern Realities, Parley).

EnableWellTrainedAssistant.Name: Enable Well-trained Automation
EnableWellTrainedAssistant.Hint: When the Ranger's Well-trained move is triggered, prompts the player to pick one training they don't already have from the "choose as many trainings as Cunning" list in the Animal Companion move's own description, and adds it to the animal companion's training list. Requires Animal Companion to have already been set up so the training list can be read.

EnableUnnaturalAllyAssistant.Name: Enable Unnatural Ally Automation
EnableUnnaturalAllyAssistant.Hint: When the Ranger's advanced move Unnatural Ally is triggered, adds +2 ferocity/+1 instinct to the Animal Companion's base stats and, the same way Well-trained does, prompts the player to pick one training they don't already have and adds it to the animal companion's training list. Requires the Animal Companion's base stats to already be set, and only applies once per character.

EnableAidOrInterfereAssistant.Name: Enable Aid or Interfere Automation
EnableAidOrInterfereAssistant.Hint: Before rolling the core Aid or Interfere move, prompts for a target and a choice between Aid (+1) or Interfere (-2). On a hit (7+), that bonus is automatically applied to the target's next roll (applied once when they actually roll, then cleared); if you lack permission over the target actor, requests approval from an online GM. If you chose Interfere and the target meets the Ranger Command's cooperating conditions, a popup asks the GM to tell the interfering player to add the animal's Instinct bonus by hand before rolling (the dungeonworld system can't apply external bonuses to a Bond roll automatically, so it has to go directly into the bond input field) — the bond input won't appear until the GM confirms.

EnableArcaneArtAssistant.Name: Enable Arcane Art Automation
EnableArcaneArtAssistant.Hint: When the Bard's Arcane Art hits, prompts for an ally and an effect (heal / bonus to next damage / clear an enchantment / enhance the next aid) and actually applies it. A 7-9 is a narrative call (unwanted attention, etc.) so it's only logged, not automated.

ArcaneArtHealIndex.Name: Arcane Art - Heal Option Index
ArcaneArtHealIndex.Hint: Which option in the list is "heal 1d8 damage" (1st in the default dungeonworld order). Specified as a number since matching by text would break under translation.

ArcaneArtDamageForwardIndex.Name: Arcane Art - Damage Bonus Option Index
ArcaneArtDamageForwardIndex.Hint: Which option in the list is "+1d4 to the next damage they deal" (2nd in the default order).

ArcaneArtClearEnchantmentIndex.Name: Arcane Art - Clear Enchantment Option Index
ArcaneArtClearEnchantmentIndex.Hint: Which option in the list is "one enchantment on their mind is cleared" (3rd in the default order). No state actually changes — this just logs a chat note.

ArcaneArtEnhanceAidIndex.Name: Arcane Art - Enhance Aid Option Index
ArcaneArtEnhanceAidIndex.Hint: Which option in the list is "the next time someone aids the target, they get +2 instead of +1" (4th in the default order). Ties into Aid or Interfere Automation.

EnableSelfForwardAssistant.Name: Enable Self-Forward Move Automation
EnableSelfForwardAssistant.Hint: When a move like Reaper (Cleric) / Quick Study (Wizard) / An Ear For Magic, Unforgettable Face (Bard) / My Love For You Is Like A Truck, Usurper (Barbarian) — "when X happens (no roll), take +1 forward" — is triggered, automatically queues that +1 for your next roll (or, for moves restricted to a specific move in the table, only that move's next roll). A badge next to the move shows whether it's currently queued, and the GM can click it to toggle on/off directly (players can only see it) — for Unforgettable Face/Usurper, where the +1 only applies against a specific NPC (or their underlings), the GM judges whether the situation applies and flips the badge accordingly.

SelfForwardMovesMenu.Name: Self-Forward Moves
SelfForwardMovesMenu.Label: Edit Self-Forward Moves
SelfForwardMovesMenu.Hint: Register by name and an optional move restriction (leave blank to apply to any next roll).

EnableBarbarianAssistant.Name: Enable Barbarian Automation
EnableBarbarianAssistant.Hint: Enables all Barbarian moves this module automates (A Good Day To Die, Samson, etc.) at once. With A Good Day To Die, +1 ongoing is automatically applied to every roll while current HP is less than CON (or 1, whichever is higher; not announced in chat). Triggering Samson pops up a debility-choice dialog.

GoodDayToDieMoveNames.Name: A Good Day To Die Move Names
GoodDayToDieMoveNames.Hint: Comma-separated list (default: A Good Day To Die).

EnableInvigorateAssistant.Name: Enable Invigorate Automation
EnableInvigorateAssistant.Hint: If the character has the Cleric's Invigorate, every time they heal someone (through any healing path this module handles — moves, spells, Balance spending, etc.) the target automatically gets "+2 forward to their next damage".

EnableLittleHelpAssistant.Name: Enable A Little Help From My Friends Automation
EnableLittleHelpAssistant.Hint: If the character has the Bard's A Little Help From My Friends, successfully choosing Aid (+1) on Aid or Interfere automatically queues +1 forward on their own next roll too (separate from the +1 queued for the person they aided). Requires "Aid or Interfere Automation" to also be enabled.

LittleHelpMoveNames.Name: A Little Help From My Friends Move Names
LittleHelpMoveNames.Hint: Comma-separated list (default: A Little Help From My Friends).

EnableIAmTheLawAssistant.Name: Enable I Am The Law Automation
EnableIAmTheLawAssistant.Hint: Queues a forward bonus for the Paladin's next roll "against that NPC", based on the I Am The Law (roll+CHA) outcome: +1 on a success (10+), -1 on a failure. Unlike Aid or Interfere, this restriction is actually enforced instead of simplified away: right after the roll, only a "bonus pending" badge lights up next to the move. While pending, every roll this character makes asks "is this roll against that NPC?" — answering yes applies the bonus to that roll and clears the pending state. Trying to roll I Am The Law again while a bonus is still pending is blocked until it's resolved. The GM can also click the badge to cancel a pending bonus. A partial success (7-9) has no mechanical effect, so only a reminder is shown.

IAmTheLawMoveNames.Name: I Am The Law Move Names
IAmTheLawMoveNames.Hint: Comma-separated list (default: I Am The Law).

EnableKnowItAllAssistant.Name: Enable Know-It-All Automation
EnableKnowItAllAssistant.Hint: When the Wizard's Know-It-All is triggered, prompts them to pick another player's character to advise. Every roll that character makes afterward asks "was this roll following that advice?" — yes grants +1 forward to that roll and marks experience for the Wizard. If the current client lacks write permission on the target/Wizard actor, an online GM is asked to approve.

EnableEncumbranceAssistant.Name: Enable Encumbrance Automation
EnableEncumbranceAssistant.Hint: Compares current load against max load on every roll and applies a penalty automatically. At or under max: no effect. Over by 1-2: a quiet -1 (stays until you shed weight). Over by 3+: before the roll, asks whether you want to drop something — dropping at least 1 weight still gives -1 and lets the roll proceed; declining (or having nothing to drop) doesn't cancel the roll — instead a huge negative modifier is added so the roll actually happens, producing the system's own success/partial/failure result card (mark-XP button included).

EnableRecruitAssistant.Name: Enable Recruit Automation
EnableRecruitAssistant.Hint: When a Recruit roll comes back a failure (6-), asks "Do you turn away everyone the GM offered?" — answering yes queues a -1 for your next Recruit roll. Recruit is a Bond roll, so rollMod can't apply it automatically (same system limitation as Aid or Interfere); instead, right before your next Recruit roll, a reminder pops up telling you to enter -1 directly in the bond input that's about to appear.

EnableBolsterAssistant.Name: Enable Bolster Automation
EnableBolsterAssistant.Hint: Triggering Bolster asks how much preparation you gained (up to 3) and adds it to a badge next to the move on the sheet (the GM can click the badge to set the value directly). While the "ask every roll" toggle (either the player or GM can flip it) is on, having any preparation means every roll asks "spend preparation?" — saying yes gives that roll +1 and spends 1 preparation.

EnableBurningBrandAssistant.Name: Enable Burning Brand Automation
EnableBurningBrandAssistant.Hint: Triggering Burning Brand prompts extra tags based on the result tier (2 on a success, 1 on a partial, 0 on a failure) and creates a weapon item in the inventory with them added to the fiery/touch/dangerous/3 uses base tags. Every attack with that weapon (melee or ranged) reduces its "N uses" tag by 1, and it's removed once it hits 0 (the Attack Assistant setting must also be enabled).

EnableVitalsAssistant.Name: Enable Max HP/Load Recalculation Buttons
EnableVitalsAssistant.Hint: Same idea as the armor recalculation button: turns the sheet's HP and Weight labels into clickable buttons. Clicking one applies class base + Constitution score for max HP, and class base + Strength modifier for base load (matching the dungeonworld system's own class-selection calculation exactly — HP and load intentionally use different formulas). Hovering shows the formula first. If the sheet's class field is empty or unrecognized, only a warning is shown and nothing changes.

EnableDefendAssistant.Name: Enable Defend Automation
EnableDefendAssistant.Hint: Triggering Defend grants a reserve (hold) based on the result tier (3 on a 10+, 1 on a 7-9, 0 on a failure) and prompts you to choose who to protect. As long as reserve remains, every time you or your ward takes damage you may spend 1 reserve to choose one of: [do nothing this time / release your stance and give up all reserve / take the hit yourself instead / halve the damage or effect / open the attacker up so an ally gets +1 forward against them / deal damage equal to your level back to the attacker].

Npc.RollButtonTitle: Randomly re-roll this NPC's name, instinct, and trait. Can be repeated any number of times.

Monster.BuildButtonTitle: Walks through the "Making a Monster" procedure from the Korean public-domain edition's Monsters chapter, answering questions to build this NPC's damage/armor/HP/tags. (The question text and tag labels are shown in Korean, matching the sourced rulebook content — same as the Instinct/Trait random tables.)
Monster.RollTreasureButtonTitle: Rolls this monster's damage die against the 1-18 treasure table. Requires running "Build Monster" at least once first.
Monster.TreasureTraveling: Is it traveling? (add at least one ration)
Monster.TreasureLeader: Is it a leader of other monsters? (+1d4)
Monster.NoDamageDieYet: Run "Build Monster" at least once before rolling treasure.
Monster.TreasureNoteMagic: Magical: carries one unusual item (possibly magic).

TagSettings.Title: Damage Tag Automation
TagSettings.Hint: If a checked tag is present on the weapon, its raw text is shown in the damage roll message. Tags marked "auto-applied by the damage buttons" (damage bonus / piercing / ignores armor) are picked up by Dungeon World's own full/half/double/heal damage-apply buttons when clicked — the system reads the message text itself; this module doesn't calculate anything. Those buttons apply to whichever tokens are selected on the canvas (not targeted), and require the Dungeon World system setting "Enable Damage Buttons" to be on (default: on). Tags marked "shown as a note only" (Forceful/Messy) have no system automation, so they're just displayed for the GM to judge.

HitTriggerMoves.Title: Hit-Taken Moves
HitTriggerMoves.Hint: Enter the move name exactly as it appears in your game (translated, if applicable). "Effect" decides what the player gives up to negate the damage: lower armor by 1, take a debility of their choice (if all 6 debilities are already taken, the move can't be used and won't be offered), end one currently-maintained ongoing spell and reduce the damage by only that spell's level (the Wizard's Spell Defense — not full negation, and unusable if no ongoing spell is currently maintained), spend one hold for full negation (the Cleric's Divine Intervention/Invincibility — unusable at 0 hold; hold is filled in whenever "Commune" is triggered, per the amount set in the Hold Grant Moves setting), or let your animal companion take the blow for full negation (the Ranger's Man's Best Friend — unusable once already spent; "after a few hours of rest it returns to normal" can't be auto-detected, so click the sheet badge to reset it manually). Check "Grants +1 forward" for moves like Armored Perfection that also grant a bonus (Dungeon World's own forward attribute, auto-applied to the next roll and then cleared; meaningless for the Spell Defense/hold/animalCompanion rows).

DamageReductionMoves.Title: Conditional Armor Bonus Moves
DamageReductionMoves.Hint: Enter the move name exactly as it appears in your game (translated, if applicable). "Base Bonus" is the armor bonus granted while the condition is not met; "Bonus When Condition Met" is granted instead while it is. Leave "Linked Move Name" blank to manage the condition with a manual per-character toggle on the move's sheet badge (for conditions independent of any other move/state, e.g. being outnumbered, feet on the ground). If the condition is exactly "is this other specific move currently active" (e.g. Paladin Holy Protection while on a Quest), enter that move's name (e.g. Quest) instead — the toggle disappears and the condition follows that move's activation state automatically. Enabling "Auto-Check: Prepared Spell" (for the Wizard's Arcane Ward/Arcane Armor) checks directly whether the character has at least one 1st-level-or-higher spell currently prepared — no manual toggle or linked move needed, it reads the state the Spell Preparation feature already maintains. Feeds into the armor recalculation button either way.

ClassGrantMoves.Title: Class Grant Moves
ClassGrantMoves.Hint: Enter the move name exactly as it appears in your game (translated, if applicable). "Fixed" mode: actually triggering "Move Name" looks up the moves listed in "Granted Move Names" (comma separated) across all 8 core class compendiums and adds them outright. "Free Choice" mode: triggering it prompts for a class, then a move from that class's list, and grants whichever is chosen (for Multiclass Dabbler/Initiate — "Granted Move Names" is unused in this mode). "Restrict Choice" accepts comma-separated class-pack keywords in English lowercase (e.g. fighter,bard,thief) to limit which classes' lists can be picked from; leave blank to allow all 8 classes (used for the Barbarian's Appetite For Destruction/Kill 'Em All, which are restricted to Fighter/Bard/Thief). "Exclude Multiclass Moves" removes Multiclass Dabbler/Initiate themselves from the pickable list. Either way, a move the character already has is not added again.
